questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Moldova?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Moldova article.

questions.proof: The capital of Moldova is Chișinău.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Moldova?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Moldova on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Moldova article.

questions.proof: It borders Ukraine to the east and Romania to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Moldova?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Moldova article.

questions.proof: The official language in Moldova is the Romanian language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Infrastructure: As of 2024, _____ has stopped selling gas to Moldova.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “stopped”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Moldova article.

questions.proof: Infrastructure: As of 2024, Russia has stopped selling gas to Moldova.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Russian Empire took almost half of the Principality of Moldova in _____ and called it Bessarabia.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Moldova article.

questions.proof: The Russian Empire took almost half of the Principality of Moldova in 1812 and called it Bessarabia.
